newsitem.title: USA: Dole takes scenic bus tour through crucial Ohio.
newsitem.headline: Dole takes scenic bus tour through crucial Ohio.

text.p: Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole was set to take his campaign into heartland territory of Ohio on Friday, the second day of his bus tour through the state he badly needs to win in November.

Whether stopping at a small town bakery that boasts it makes the world's biggest pumpkin pie, standing in the shadow of grain silos or bathed in the light of the ferris wheel at a county fair, Dole has pushed his message of cutting taxes, fighting drugs and promising to be more trustworthy than his opponent, President Bill Clinton.

He seemed to be enjoying himself, appearing very animated at some rallies, and telling jokes using the microphone from the window of his bus, "Asphalt One" -- a play on the presidential jet Air Force One.
"Thanks for the milkshake," he said as his bus left the town of Lebanon in one leg of his two-day tour, which on Friday will take him to diners, campuses and small towns in Ohio.

Ohio has 21 electoral votes and was seen as a "must-win" state for Dole. Although most of the top state officials are Republicans, Dole trails in the polls here. Clinton won a narrow victory in Ohio in 1992 and he also campaigned here on Thursday.

Most of Dole's Ohio events have been in Republican regions and he acknowledged that the trip was aimed at solidifying his base. Dole will have to win over many of the swing voters who are not rock solid Republicans in order to win Ohio.
